key_insight: A latent diffusion model can generate functional humanoid control policies directly in weight space, and the learned weights appear to encode a shared kinematic prior across training paradigms.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a new route for synthesizing deployable robot controllers and for interpreting which structural features of policy weights are tied to humanoid embodiment.
method: Train a linear autoencoder to compress actor-network parameters into a latent space.
Use a Diffusion Transformer to model and sample the latent weight distribution.
Decode sampled latents back into full control networks for deployment and analysis.
evidence_signal: The model was trained on RL-derived networks from the Unitree G1 and produced real-world policies capable of walking, dancing, and spin kicks, while analysis revealed a consistent first-layer structural pattern linked to kinematic priors under both RL and IL.
watch_item: Generative weight-space models may produce deployable controllers only if the training set is sufficiently diverse and the decoded weights preserve safety and stability under real-world robot dynamics.
paper_title: Modeling and Understanding Neural Weights of Humanoid Policies with Diffusion
